specification.objective: Add a persistent per-project Kanban using Task as the canonical card, with ordered encrypted columns, monotonic human card numbers, safe concurrent ordering, project-scoped assignees, tenant isolation, and role-aware Flutter interaction.

requirements.statement: Each project exposes an isolated Kanban snapshot; managerial roles may access same-company projects without EmployeeProject, while employees require project membership.
Task remains the canonical card and gains an immutable per-project card number plus persisted Kanban column and position.
Project owns next_card_number and kanban_version; card numbers are unique per project, monotonic, concurrency-safe and never reused after deletion.
KanbanColumn is project-owned, ordered, encrypted, manager-administered and never deletable while non-empty or when it is the last column.
Card move/reorder and column reorder use expectedVersion, serialize on Project, normalize contiguous positions, increment kanban_version, and reject stale writes with 409.
TaskEmployee remains the assignee model and project.task_employee_limit remains the backend-enforced capacity; employees may manage Kanban assignees only for cards in projects they belong to.
Legacy Task create/update/list contracts remain compatible; old task creation places the task in the system initial column and does not weaken existing hierarchy or encryption rules.
Flutter represents the authoritative board snapshot, exposes a project Kanban entry, supports native drag/drop intents, gates actions by role, and reloads after 409 conflicts.
Schema upgrade backfills existing projects/tasks deterministically and idempotently, creating an initial A fazer column and assigning card numbers by created_at,id.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Manager without membership can read and mutate same-company Kanban; employee requires membership and cannot administer columns or textual card content.
Two projects may each have card #1, one project cannot duplicate a card number, and deleted numbers are not reused.
A stale expectedVersion fails with 409 and accepted move/reorder persists contiguous positions after reload.
Only project members can be assigned and capacity remains enforced by the backend.
Legacy schema upgrades preserve tasks and assign each migrated task a stable number, valid column and position on repeated upgrade.
Legacy Task APIs remain accepted and return additive cardNumber, kanbanColumnId and kanbanPosition fields.
Flutter contracts/controller/widgets represent ordered columns/cards, role gating, drag/drop mutation intents and conflict reload semantics.
Managers can create, rename, reorder and conservatively delete columns; employees cannot administer structure; non-empty and last-column deletion fail with 409.

invariants.statement: All Project access remains scoped by company_id before project membership or role checks.
Task UUID, type, parent_task_id, encryption, timestamps and hierarchy remain authoritative.
Removing an EmployeeProject continues removing TaskEmployee links for that project.
No Kanban mutation trusts client-supplied task, column or employee IDs without validating same project/company ownership.

forbidden_states.statement: A card exists without a project-valid column, duplicate card number, or non-contiguous persisted position.
A stale board mutation silently overwrites an accepted newer mutation.
An employee outside a project can read or mutate its Kanban or become an assignee.
Deleting a column or card implicitly orphans cards or child tasks.

inputs.statement: Authenticated company/user context, project IDs, task/card IDs, column IDs, employee IDs and expected Kanban version.
Existing Project, Task, EmployeeProject and TaskEmployee rows during schema upgrade.

outputs.statement: Authorized ordered Kanban snapshots with version, columns, cards and assignees.
Persisted, conflict-safe card/column lifecycle mutations with explicit 409 on stale state.

failure_semantics.statement: Stale expectedVersion mutations fail with HTTP 409 and no partial ordering change is committed.
Cross-company, cross-project and invalid membership identifiers fail closed without exposing foreign data.
Deleting the last or a non-empty column, or deleting a task with children, fails with conflict and preserves data.
If Flutter tooling is unavailable locally, frontend tests are not claimed as passed; source changes remain subject to CI flutter test.
